description.description: An independently requested content subject and its scope; mode carries the required/forbidden polarity. Describe prohibited content itself, such as 'explanatory prose in the source text', not 'do not include explanation'. Exact copy already guarantees no changes or additions: do not create content conditions for 'copy unchanged' or 'do not add a new explanation'. Preserve conditions on the selected text itself, such as required topics or prohibited original content. Do not restate saving, sending, or the body operation as a content condition.

kind.description: Semantic content only. code means program code, code_example means an illustrative code example, and example means an illustration of any kind. A code_block is layout and can contain logs or input text. Do not repeat the body transformation, action, line count or layout as custom content. A table prohibition belongs to format.table, not comparison or custom.
kind.title: Kind

replaces.description: For a change to one pending content condition, copy its offered ref from pending_request.confirmed_facts.answer.content. Null adds an independent condition. Never invent a ref; it is valid only for the offered request revision.

PlannedRequirement.description: An independently planned subject has one match mode, never mixed symbol roles.

aspects.description: Literal parameter names, option/flag names, requested value tokens or code fragments that must appear in returned source, such as axis, --force, reflect or random_state. For both docs and upload, aspects add source-content restrictions beyond identifying the API in symbols. Questions about a call's ownership or surrounding assignments and match/case binding belong in query and the body; they do not require those terms inside the selected call. Naming an API, requiring its actual library identity, or asking to quote its source unchanged does not require that API spelling in source. A verified import alias still qualifies. Repeat a symbol here only when the user independently requires its exact spelling and would exclude aliases; retain both fields in that case. For docs setting-meaning questions, omit ordinary data and arbitrary counts, capacities, sizes, thresholds or seeds; keep their parameter names here and complete settings in query and the body request. A value changing the result is not sufficient to make it a literal anchor. Keep categorical modes, enum members, sentinels and distinct behavior-branch values separately alongside their parameter names, including numeric or Boolean choices. Preserve an explicitly requested exact source/code match. Source locations (lines/ranges, cells, pages or document regions) belong in query and the body request, not aspects, unless explicitly requested as literal strings occurring in source. Classify by the requested role, even when location labels are quoted. For upload and docs, never put natural-language properties or conditions here; preserve their meaning in query. For docs additionally request the relevant evidence_needs. Only anchors explicitly requested in the user's dialogue belong here; never guess an identifier from the user's description of a property.
aspects.title: Aspects

evidence_needs.description: Docs-only evidence kinds requested by the user: signature for call syntax, parameters for option/argument descriptions, examples for usage examples, explanation for conceptual or behavioral explanation. A broad request to explain API usage needs explanation; it does not require all four kinds or examples copied from the documentation. Explaining a named parameter setting requests BOTH parameters and explanation, even when phrased as its behavior or effect; that value needs the parameter's own description. Keep empty for upload. Do not infer unrelated kinds from model knowledge.
evidence_needs.title: Evidence Needs

file_ids.description: Upload file IDs from the active catalog whose evidence is explicitly requested. Empty searches all active uploads without requiring every file in the answer. For a comparison or inspection of all attachments, include every requested file ID in one task. Empty for docs.
file_ids.title: File Ids

library.description: Exact canonical owning-library ID for official docs. Use unsupported for an explicitly requested library outside the enum; preserve its actual name in query/symbols. Python owns standard-library modules such as pathlib. Never append module names, versions or prose to this ID. Null for upload or an unscoped docs subject.
library.title: Library

match.description: topic for broad explanation; symbol for API/usage references, including an uploaded function's implementation together with its actual calls/examples; definition when only the named uploaded function/class implementation is needed. A definition alone excludes calls outside its body.
match.title: Match

symbols.description: At most one primary target. Use a fully qualified API name when selecting calls to that API. To investigate whether an uploaded call belongs to that API, use the observed call's written name instead; do not assume the answer by canonicalizing its owner. Preserve ownership and surrounding binding questions in query and the body, not as additional literal aspects. Use separate tasks for independent symbols, including each uploaded variable/constant whose value is requested. Never put a second independent variable in the first variable's aspects: symbol retrieval selects only the primary target's occurrences. A query mentioning related samples, constraints, writes or other objects does not widen those occurrences. Plan a separate target when its name is known, or an explicit topic task without symbols when the related source must be discovered. Calls inspected inside a function belong in its aspects, not additional definitions.
symbols.title: Symbols

version.description: One exact requested version token, for example 3.12, 1.26, v2.4 or latest. For 'Python 3.12', return only '3.12'. Never include a library name, spaces, prose or an inferred default version. Null when the user did not constrain the version.

200.description:
UTF-8 SSE frames: event: <name>
data: <JSON object>

. Each execution ends with one final_response carrying status, response, problem, message, execution_id, trace, debug and upload_manifest. Status distinguishes completed, needs_input, failed, partial and refused; a failed result has no answer document. The manifest is captured under the session lock; null on failure means unknown state, not an empty attachment set. HTTP 200 and done alone do not indicate success. Clients must not automatically resubmit interrupted requests because agent actions may already have executed. x-sse-events maps each event name to its data schema.
